facts.statement: Jeyawati is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur whose name means "grinding mouth" in the Zuni language.
facts.quote: Jeyawati (meaning "grinding mouth" in the Zuni language) is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur which lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The type species Jeyawati rugoculus was formally described in 2010 based on fossils found in New Mexico.
facts.quote: The type species, J. rugoculus, was described in 2010, based on fossils recovered in the U.S. state of New Mexico.

facts.statement: Fossils of Jeyawati rugoculus were discovered in 1996 in the Moreno Hill Formation in western New Mexico.
facts.quote: The fossil remains of Jeyawati rugoculus were discovered in 1996 in western New Mexico, in rocks of the Moreno Hill Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found by Douglas G. Wolfe, Hazel Wolfe, and Christopher Wolfe during the Zuni Basin Paleontological Project.
facts.quote: The partial skull and associated postcranial fragments were discovered by paleontologist Douglas G. Wolfe, his wife Hazel Wolfe, and their son Christopher Wolfe during work associated with the Zuni Basin Paleontological Project.

facts.statement: Excavation and collection of the specimen continued for about 13 years with help from James I. Kirkland and volunteers.
facts.quote: Following the discovery, excavation and collection of the specimen continued for approximately 13 years, with contributions from James I. Kirkland, volunteers of the Southwest Paleontological Society, and other participants.

facts.statement: Andrew T. McDonald, Douglas G. Wolfe, and James I. Kirkland formally described the species in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology in 2010.
facts.quote: The new genus and species, Jeyawati rugoculus, was formally described by McDonald, Wolfe and Kirkland in 2010 in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

facts.statement: Jeyawati is known from an incomplete skeleton consisting of disarticulated skull parts and fragmentary postcranial bones.
facts.quote: Jeyawati is a basal hadrosauroid dinosaur known from an incomplete skeleton, including disarticulated skull elements and fragmentary postcranial material.

facts.statement: The species is distinguished by a rough texture on the side of the postorbital bone and a large opening at the base of its jugal process.
facts.quote: The species is distinguished by a rugose (rough) texture covering the lateral surface of the postorbital, together with a large neurovascular foramen at the base of the jugal process of the postorbital and a distinctive combination of other anatomical characters.

facts.statement: The species name refers to its chewing adaptations and the wrinkled texture of the bone around the eye.
facts.quote: Its name, meaning approximately "grinding mouth, wrinkle eye," refers to its chewing adaptations and the unusual wrinkled texture of the bone surrounding the eye.

facts.statement: Jeyawati possessed primitive features in its teeth and jaws alongside characteristics of the hadrosauroid lineage.
facts.quote: Jeyawati possessed primitive features of the teeth and jaws while showing characteristics associated with the hadrosauroid lineage.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis indicates Jeyawati was more primitive than Shuangmiaosaurus, Telmatosaurus, and Bactrosaurus, but more advanced than Eolambia, Probactrosaurus, and Protohadros.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico indica que Jeyawati era más primitivo que Shuangmiaosaurus, Telmatosaurus y Bactrosaurus, pero más avanzado que Eolambia, Probactrosaurus y Protohadros.

facts.statement: Jeyawati lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Jeyawati (meaning "grinding mouth" in the Zuni language) is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur which lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Jeyawati lived in North America approximately 97 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 97 durante el Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Jeyawati is estimated between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Jeyawati belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
The genus authority is cited as Wolfe & Kirkland, 2010.
